passages.scripture: Therefore, while the promise of entering His rest still stands, let us be careful that none of you be deemed to have fallen short of it.

lines.text: The promise of entering God's rest still stands.
So we must be careful.
None of you should be found to have fallen short of God's rest.

passages.scripture: For we also received the good news just as they did; but the message they heard was of no value to them, since they did not share the faith of those who comprehended it.

lines.text: For we have received the good news, just as the Israelites did.
But the message the Israelites heard did not benefit them.
The Israelites did not share the faith of those who truly believed the good news.

passages.scripture: Now we who have believed enter that rest. As for the others, it is just as God has said: “So I swore on oath in My anger, ‘They shall never enter My rest.’ ” And yet His works have been finished since the foundation of the world.

lines.text: Now we who have believed enter God's rest.
As for the others, God has said:
"So in My anger I swore that they would never enter My rest."
And yet God's works have been finished since the foundation of the world.

passages.scripture: For somewhere He has spoken about the seventh day in this manner: “And on the seventh day God rested from all His works.”

lines.text: For God has spoken this somewhere about the seventh day:
"And on the seventh day God rested from all His works."

passages.scripture: And again, as He says in the passage above: “They shall never enter My rest.”

lines.text: And again God says in the passage above:
"They shall never enter My rest."

passages.scripture: Since, then, it remains for some to enter His rest, and since those who formerly heard the good news did not enter because of their disobedience, God again designated a certain day as “Today,” when a long time later He spoke through David as was just stated: “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts.”

lines.text: So God's rest still remains for some to enter.
And the Israelites long ago also heard the good news.
But the Israelites did not enter, because they disobeyed.
So God again set a certain day, and called it “Today.”
Long afterward, God spoke through David, as already quoted:
“Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts.”

passages.scripture: For if Joshua had given them rest, God would not have spoken later about another day.

lines.text: Suppose Joshua had given the Israelites rest in the land.
Then God would not have spoken later about entering another day of rest.

passages.scripture: There remains, then, a Sabbath rest for the people of God.

lines.text: So then, a Sabbath rest still remains — a rest like God's own rest after creation, which we enter fully when Jesus returns.
This rest is for the people of God.

passages.scripture: For whoever enters God’s rest also rests from his own work, just as God did from His.

lines.text: Whoever enters God's rest also rests from their own work — eventually, we will rest from our good works done through faith in this life.
God did the same, resting from His own work.

passages.scripture: Let us, therefore, make every effort to enter that rest, so that no one will fall by following the same pattern of disobedience.

lines.text: In the wilderness, the Israelites disobeyed God, leaving a pattern of disobedience.
So let us make every effort to enter God's rest.
Then none of us will fall by following that same pattern.

passages.scripture: For the word of God is living and active. Sharper than any double-edged sword, it pierces even to dividing soul and spirit, joints and marrow. It judges the thoughts and intentions of the heart.

lines.text: For God's word is living.
And God's word is active.
God's word is sharper than any double-edged sword.
God's word pierces so deep it divides soul and spirit.
God's word even divides joints and marrow.
God's word judges the thoughts of the heart.
God's word judges the intentions of the heart.

passages.scripture: Nothing in all creation is hidden from God’s sight; everything is uncovered and exposed before the eyes of Him to whom we must give account.

lines.text: Nothing in all creation is hidden from God's sight.
Everything is uncovered and exposed before God's eyes.
And we must give an account to God.

passages.scripture: Therefore, since we have a great high priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold firmly to what we profess.

lines.text: We have a great high priest — our representative before God.
This great high priest has passed through the heavens to God.
This great high priest is Jesus, the Son of God.
So let us hold firmly to the faith we confess.

passages.scripture: For we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but we have one who was tempted in every way that we are, yet was without sin.

lines.text: Our high priest is able to sympathize with our weaknesses.
For Jesus was tempted in every way, just as we are.
Yet Jesus never sinned.

passages.scripture: Let us then approach the throne of grace with confidence, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help us in our time of need.

lines.text: God has a throne of grace.
We approach God's throne of grace through prayer.
Jesus, our great High Priest, intercedes as we approach the throne of grace.
The Holy Spirit also intercedes for us as we approach God's throne — with groanings too deep for words.
Even if we approach the throne of grace in weakness or sin, Jesus and the Spirit make our imperfect prayers perfectly acceptable to God.
So let us approach God's throne of grace with confidence.
At the throne of grace we receive mercy when we have sinned.
And we find grace to help us in our time of need — to resist sin and obey God.
